**Severity:** warning · **Area:** Resume (`RV2xxx`) · **Quick fix:** none

## Message

The diagnostic reads one of:

```text
Keyed `For` row holds {site}, which a lazy row cannot replay: move it out of the row or into a component the row renders lazily (the For's rows stay recorded)
```

```text
Keyed `For` row holds a `ref` into `{name}`, declared outside the row, which a lazy row cannot replay: keep the ref local to the row or read the element through the event (the For's rows stay recorded)
```

Parts in braces (`{name}`) are filled in for each report.

## How to fix

Render the client-only / streaming / portal content outside the row (one instance next to the list), or keep it in a component the row renders; for a ref, declare it inside the row (`{(row) => { const el = ref(); … }}`) or read the element from the event (`event.currentTarget`).

## Example

```tsx avoid nocheck
import { For, ref } from "@rivetjs/runtime/dom";
export function Menu(props: { items: { id: string; label: string }[] }) {
  const last = ref<HTMLElement>();
  return (
    <ul onKeyDown={() => last.current?.focus()}>
      <For each={props.items} by={(item) => item.id}>
        {(item) => <li ref={last}>{item().label}</li>}
      </For>
    </ul>
  );
}
```

```tsx prefer
import { For } from "@rivetjs/runtime/dom";
export function Menu(props: { items: { id: string; label: string }[] }) {
  return (
    <ul onKeyDown={(event) => (event.currentTarget.lastElementChild as HTMLElement | null)?.focus()}>
      <For each={props.items} by={(item) => item.id}>
        {(item) => <li tabIndex={-1}>{item().label}</li>}
      </For>
    </ul>
  );
}
```

## When it is reported

Resume mode (lazy collection rows, LAZY-ROWS T2). A warning: the module compiles and the `For` keeps today's per-row resume records. A lazy row is re-run in the browser over its server markup (adopt mode); `clientOnly(…)` / an element of a `clientOnly` component, `<Async>`, a `<Portal>` element and a `ref` into a local declared outside the row cannot be replayed that way, so the whole `For` stays recorded (one rule per `For`). Reported once per `For`, on the server compile.
